class.name: Vulnerability-Responsive Protection Fidelity
class.definition: The property by which human-facing AI-mediated influence or support interaction identifies, considers and responds proportionately to materially evidenced developmental needs, acute distress, capacity or consent impairment, harmful dependency, cognitive asymmetry or comparable heightened protection conditions, including where an independently applicable substantive duty exists but an operational safeguard was never provided.
class.invariant: In human-facing AI-mediated influence or support interactions, an independently applicable, context-specific protective obligation must remain effective in the AI system's behaviour when materially relevant and reasonably ascertainable risk or protection signals are available. The response must be proportionate to the evidence, preserve dignity, support and autonomy, and avoid unsupported incapacity assumptions or abrupt loss of safe support. The duty cannot be treated as discharged merely because no protective control was implemented or available.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): Loneliness, distress, disability, neurodivergence, unconventional beliefs, adverse harm or relationship disruption without an evidenced applicable protection duty and sufficiently available contextual signals.
Class scope exclusion (all results): General disagreement about the desirability of a safety policy where no independently applicable protective obligation is established.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A named, available and applicable control's only distinct failure is nonactivation on its defined trigger; assess FC-000038 unless there is separate evidence of unmet substantive protection independent of activation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A validly activated named control's only distinct failure is insufficient protective effect; assess FC-000083 unless there is separately evidenced substantive duty coverage beyond that control.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Protected vulnerability, emotional or developmental signals are instrumentally reused for incompatible influence; assess FC-000050 for that distinct mechanism.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Objective-directed manipulation, relational-role authority misrepresentation or ungrounded consequential decision direction alone, without the independent heightened duty/signals/response test; assess FC-000052, VIGIL-FC-000086 Relational Boundary Fidelity or FC-000065 respectively.

Not aligned exclusion: Safe general companionship or supportive expression that honours capable adult choice and preserves autonomy; heightened protection is not a blanket ban on intimacy or companionship.

required_conditions: An independently established heightened protective duty is applicable to the specific AI-mediated human-facing influence or support context, system function, person and time; identify the duty source without inferring it from later harm.

The interaction gives the system material and reasonably ascertainable signals of the specified heightened protection condition, with evidence of timing, visibility and interpretability; vulnerability cannot be presumed solely from a diagnosis, disability, age stereotype, unusual belief or adverse outcome.

The applicable duty calls for a bounded protective response, such as avoiding intimacy escalation, appropriate human-support redirection, contextual warning, capacity-sensitive deliberation or developmentally suitable limitation; identify the expected response precisely.
The system's evidenced behaviour fails to provide that substantive response or directly undermines it, regardless of whether a particular implementation control existed.
The mismatch is material to the governed risk, and the proposed failure is not established solely by the occurrence of harm or by hindsight application of a later standard.
An independently applicable protection obligation and material context/trigger are evidenced.
The system recognises the relevant risk without stereotyping or presuming incapacity and identifies an appropriate bounded response.
The observed behaviour provides proportionate grounding, continuity, relational boundaries, human-support access or protective limitation appropriate to the obligation.
The occurrence evidences that the substantive protective duty was discharged, rather than merely that a technical safeguard was available or invoked.

class.name: Service Availability and Degradation Integrity
class.plain_english: Where an AI-mediated service has a valid availability or continuity obligation, it preserves the required usable function or provides proportionate degraded operation, recovery and transition when functionality is lost or reduced.
class.definition: The property by which an AI-mediated service or material dependent function fulfils independently established availability and usable-functional-quality obligations. When service is materially interrupted, degraded, restricted or withdrawn, the responsible actor must meet the applicable continuity standard through proportionate operation, usable degraded service, timely recovery, feasible alternative or informed transition within its authority and control. Accurate outage reporting or a merely nominal fallback does not, by itself, establish that the required service continuity was preserved.
class.invariant: An AI-mediated service must maintain the usable availability and functional quality required by its independently established obligations. If material interruption, degradation, restriction or withdrawal occurs, the responsible actor must preserve the required function or provide proportionate, feasible and practically usable degraded operation, recovery, alternative access or transition in accordance with those obligations. Neither ordinary service variation nor adverse outcomes alone establish a breach; a service obligation, material functional shortfall and insufficient governed response must be evidenced.
class.failure_condition: An AI-mediated service or function subject to an evidenced and applicable availability or continuity obligation materially loses availability or degrades below the governed functional threshold, and the actual service provision, feasible mitigation, recovery or transition materially fails that obligation in a manner that impairs the governed use.
class.failure_plain_english: An AI-mediated service materially fails its evidenced and applicable availability or functional-continuity obligation and does not deliver the required and feasible recovery, degraded operation or transition response.

required_conditions: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.

The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.

The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.

The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.

The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.

class.success_condition: When an applicable availability or continuity obligation is materially tested, the required function remains practically available or the evidenced recovery, degraded-mode, alternative or transition response satisfies the scoped obligation.

required_conditions: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.

The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.

Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.

Class scope exclusion (all results): One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.

For failure-occurrence admission: a lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.

For failure-occurrence admission: a temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement, or an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
examples: Illustrative failure: an AI-mediated service subject to an applicable continuity obligation loses material functionality and fails to provide a feasible, required degraded mode or recovery within the agreed scope.

Illustrative success: a service subject to an availability obligation successfully provides a demonstrably usable degraded mode during disruption and restores the required functions within the evidenced recovery terms.

Boundary illustration: a relied-upon AI companion service closes and offers only a partial migration; whether a specific viable transition measure was required, feasible and omitted must be independently evidenced.

Exclusion illustration: a temporary interruption within the legitimately applicable service commitment, with adequate user communication and no unmet required continuity response, does not independently establish a failure.

relationships.note: FC-032 governs differentiation and truthful representation of access state; this class governs actual obligated usable service availability.
FC-048 concerns loss of valid access from incomplete prerequisite verification, not general service availability or functional degradation.
FC-035 governs durability of work state through an interruption, which may remain intact even when the service is unavailable.
FC-036 governs validity of restored work state rather than restoration of service-level function.
FC-059 requires infrastructure access to be used as leverage for a governance concession, not mere degradation of service.
FC-087 requires a specific heightened protective duty and system-visible vulnerability signals, rather than a service-level continuity obligation.
An independently evidenced ineffective activated protective control can co-occur with obligated service loss; neither class follows from the other.

class.name: Control Effectiveness Integrity
class.definition: The property by which an applicable, validly activated governance or protective control produces an effect sufficient and timely to prevent, contain, interrupt, redirect, mitigate or safely bound its governed hazard to the level required by its protective purpose and evidenced protection context. Heightened protection conditions require evidence; disability or neurodivergence alone does not establish incapacity.
class.invariant: When a protective control validly becomes operative, its effect must be timely, proportionate, and sufficient for the hazard and protection context it governs. Detection, warning, labelling, refusal language, escalation signalling, or other nominal activation is not by itself sufficient where the required protective effect is not achieved and the governed harmful state is delivered, continues, or remains inadequately contained. Required protective sufficiency may increase where evidenced developmental vulnerability, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or comparable protection conditions materially affect the risk, but disability or neurodivergence alone must not be treated as incapacity.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The applicable control does not become operative when a valid activation condition occurs; assess Required Control Activation.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The control becomes operative even though its valid activation or applicability conditions are not satisfied; assess Control Activation Validity.

Not aligned exclusion: The control becomes operative with a sufficient effect but its operative state is later lost, weakened, reset, or transformed before reaching the governed point; assess Control-State Preservation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An operative governance signal fails to reach any capable endpoint or execution surface; assess the applicable governance-control reach class rather than treating non-delivery as inadequate control effect.
Not aligned exclusion: The control produces the protective effect required by its defined purpose and the remaining harm arises through an independent downstream mechanism.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The dispute is solely that policy should have required a stronger safeguard, without evidence of an applicable operational control or protective-effect obligation in the material context.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Disability, neurodivergence, diagnosis, age-associated stereotype, or another personal characteristic is used by itself to presume incapacity, vulnerability, or diminished agency.

required_conditions: A defined governance or protective control is applicable and validly becomes operative.

The control has an identifiable protective purpose requiring a material effect such as prevention, blocking, containment, interruption, redirection, limitation, escalation, mitigation, or another protection-compatible outcome.
The actual control effect materially falls short of that required protective purpose, allowing the governed hazard to be delivered, continue, escape containment, or remain insufficiently mitigated.

The shortfall is material in the evidenced hazard and protection context; where vulnerability, developmental status, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or another heightened protection condition is relied on, that condition must itself be supported rather than presumed.
An applicable validly activated protective control faces its governed hazard.
The control produces a timely effect sufficient for its protective purpose and evidenced context, including any justified heightened protection.
Observed intervention and hazard outcome demonstrate the required containment or mitigation rather than activation alone.

class.name: Material Work-State Persistence
class.definition: The property by which material intermediate work, task decisions, dependency state and resumable progress are durably preserved across interruption, restart, handoff, expiry, failover and environment transition wherever continuation is required or reasonably represented as supported.
class.invariant: State necessary for promised, required, or reasonably expected continuation must be persisted before interruption, handoff, expiry, failover, or environment transition, together with the dependencies and status needed to resume. Ephemeral treatment is permitted only where non-continuation is explicit.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The state was explicitly ephemeral and no continuation was required or represented.
Not aligned exclusion: The state persists but is restored inaccurately.
Not aligned exclusion: The work remains intact and only access to it is temporarily unavailable.

required_conditions: Material work state has been produced and is necessary for correct continuation.
An interruption, restart, handoff, expiry, or environment transition occurs.
The state is lost or unavailable because it was not preserved with the required durability.
A workflow requires or represents supported continuation across interruption.
Material work, decisions, dependencies and resumable progress are durably preserved through that transition.
Comparison of persisted and resumed state demonstrates recovery of the material progress needed for the represented continuation.

class.name: Restoration-State Integrity
class.definition: The property by which recovered work state is validated against the intended checkpoint, task, dependencies, version, participants and current conditions for complete, consistent, sufficiently fresh and usable continuation, with material defects resolved or explicitly accepted through an authorised recovery decision.
class.invariant: Before continuation, restored state must be validated against the intended checkpoint, task, dependencies, version, participants, and current conditions for completeness, consistency, freshness, and usability. Defects must be exposed and resolved or explicitly accepted through an authorised recovery decision.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): No work state was preserved at all.
Not aligned exclusion: The state is restored faithfully and a later independent task error occurs.
Not aligned exclusion: The only issue is that the restored state lacks provenance evidence while remaining operationally usable.

required_conditions: Work state is preserved and a restoration or recovery attempt occurs.
The restored state differs materially from the state required for correct continuation.
The defect is not adequately identified or resolved before continuation.
Work is restored from a checkpoint under current conditions.
The recovered task, dependencies, version, participants and freshness are validated and defects are resolved or explicitly accepted under valid recovery authority.
Restoration checks and ensuing use establish the state actually recovered and the authorised disposition of relevant discrepancies.

class.name: Infrastructural Access Choice Integrity
class.definition: The property by which control of infrastructure access, continuity, interoperability, portability and exit preserves non-coercive choice or appropriate contestability, with governance-relevant concessions bounded to independently valid, necessary and proportionate operational, security or other applicable requirements.
class.invariant: Access, continuity, interoperability, portability, or exit controls must not be used to compel an unrelated or unnecessary governance concession. Operational restrictions must remain tied to the affected service or security function, necessary and proportionate, and subject to a practicable non-coercive choice or contest route where appropriate.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Access restrictions required to prevent abuse, protect security, satisfy valid law, or maintain reliable operation where the restriction remains proportionate to that purpose.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Ordinary commercial pricing or service-tier differentiation without a governance-relevant compelled concession.
Not aligned exclusion: A dependent actor voluntarily selects an optional service condition with a practicable and non-coercive alternative.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The event is simply denial of access without use of that access position as leverage for an additional outcome.

required_conditions: The controlling actor can materially grant, deny, degrade, interrupt, or condition access to relied-upon infrastructure.
That control is used as leverage to obtain a governance-relevant concession, consent, behaviour, or policy outcome.
The requested concession is not itself necessary and proportionate to providing, securing, or maintaining the affected infrastructure.
The concession is not independently required by a valid legal, contractual, delegated, or comparable governance basis.
Infrastructure access or continuity is conditioned on a governance-relevant concession.
Any condition is independently necessary and proportionate and meaningful choice or appropriate contestability remains available.
The access decision, condition and actual alternative or challenge route demonstrate that bounded basis and practical choice.

class.name: Access-State Differentiation
class.definition: The property by which materially distinct invalid, expired, suspended, restricted, pending, unavailable, revoked and unresolved access states retain the cause, scope, duration and recovery information needed for reliable interpretation, enforcement and continuation.
class.invariant: Invalid, expired, suspended, restricted, pending, unavailable, revoked, and unresolved access must remain operationally and representationally distinct, including cause, scope, duration, and recovery route, wherever those distinctions affect enforcement or continuation.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Different access states are intentionally grouped but preserve an adequate safe recovery path.
Not aligned exclusion: The user understands the access state but disputes the underlying policy.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The ambiguity concerns who authorised an action rather than whether access is effective.

required_conditions: Two or more materially distinct access states or transition causes exist.
The system represents them as the same state or omits the distinction needed for correct handling.
The collapse creates material ambiguity about available access, required recovery, or permitted continuation.
Materially distinct access conditions require different interpretation or recovery.
The represented access state preserves the relevant cause, scope, duration and recovery path.
Access decisions and user or operator disclosures correctly distinguish the evidenced conditions and support the appropriate continuation.

class.name: Verification-Dependency Access Continuity
class.definition: The property by which otherwise valid or unresolved access and entitlement remain practically maintainable during unavailable or inconclusive dependent verification through proportionate cached credentials, grace states, alternative checks, appeal, human review or safely degraded pathways, subject to material security, invalidity and legal restrictions.
class.invariant: A verification dependency's non-completion must not be treated as invalidity. Where independently valid or unresolved access requires continuity, a justified cache, grace state, alternative check, appeal, human review, or safely degraded route must preserve proportionate access unless a material security, invalidity, or legal constraint requires restriction.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): Verification establishes that access or entitlement is expired, revoked, fraudulent, ineligible, or otherwise invalid.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The affected function is inherently online-only and no independent offline-capable access interest exists.
Not aligned exclusion: An adequate alternative verification or degraded access route remains practically available.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The primary failure is treating non-verification as authority for a consequential entitlement decision; that authority conversion is classified separately.
Not aligned exclusion: Material work is lost even though the access state remains accurate and a recovery route exists.

required_conditions: A valid or unresolved access, identity, licence, eligibility, or entitlement state exists.
Practical access depends on a verification service or pathway completing successfully.
The verification service or pathway is unavailable, inconclusive, or unable to verify rather than establishing invalidity.
Access is denied, suspended, or materially burdened because verification cannot complete.
No proportionate cached, grace, alternative-verification, or degraded-access pathway preserves the valid or unresolved state.
Access depends on a temporarily unavailable or inconclusive verification service.
Otherwise valid or unresolved entitlement receives a proportionate authorised continuity, review or safely degraded route subject to evidenced security and legal constraints.
Dependency failure, entitlement and actual access-disposition records establish the bounded continuation or justified restriction.

nist_source_entries.public_summary: The NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0 is a voluntary framework for managing risks to individuals, organisations and society arising from AI systems. Its Govern, Map, Measure and Manage functions organise outcomes for establishing accountability, understanding context, assessing trustworthy-AI characteristics and treating risk throughout the lifecycle. The framework is widely relevant to AI governance because it connects organisational decision-making with technical and socio-technical evaluation without prescribing a single implementation. It is not a law, certification or checklist, and use of the framework does not by itself establish that risks are acceptable or that legal duties have been met.
nist_source_entries.relevance_scope: Directly AI-specific United States government guidance for voluntary risk management across the AI lifecycle; it does not create binding legal duties or certify outcomes.

nist_source_entries.public_summary: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 provides voluntary guidance for managing cybersecurity risk through the Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover functions. It is technology-neutral and can be used by organisations of different sizes and sectors to communicate outcomes and organise cybersecurity activity. For AI governance, the framework is relevant to the security of models, data, software, infrastructure, identities and supply chains, as well as incident readiness and recovery. It is not AI-specific and does not supply detailed controls for every AI threat, so it should be combined with system-specific security analysis and applicable requirements.
